correctness.rationale: The Cayley–Hamilton projector parametrization is smooth and counts exactly 6·4^(k−1) projectors. The determinant polarization identity reduces representation to a trace-pairing fiber. Four mod-two similarity classes yield exact regular root counts and explain the exceptional primitive-scalar branch. Dyadic Hensel lifting gives every positive regular fiber and the obstructed scalar criterion, whose disjoint valuation classes number (8^(k−1)−1)/7. The minimum 2^(k+1) is attained on primitive nonscalar targets. A standalone checker enumerates the entire convolution and every target for k=2,3,4,5. Its finite range is not used as an infinite proof.

value.rationale: A natural convolution of a canonical matrix conjugacy orbit has a precise and unexpected infinite-depth support obstruction absent at the field level. The 55/56 limiting support density and sharp least positive representation count are exact global invariants with plausible use in additive harmonic estimates and projector decomposition problems. The result identifies an essential dyadic boundary to the established odd-prime full support, rather than a routine parameter replacement.
